newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Stock Exchange develops trading system.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Stock Exchange develops trading system.

text.p: The Bulgarian Stock Exchange (BSE) has developed a trading system for stocks of Bulgaria's voucher sell-off programme accessible throughout the world via Reuter Terminal workstations, the BSE board chairman said.

"The system is up and running. Now the Securities and Stock Exchange Commission has to clear legal obstacles to BSE floor trading of shares in privatised companies to avoid abuse," BSE board chairman Viktor Papazov told reporters.

The Windows NT-based BSE trading system can link up to 50 workstations to place bid and offer prices. Tests showed that the system could process 8,500 bids and offers in two hours and simulated deals were around 6,200.
The commission suspended share trading on the BSE in October because of legal tangles concerning registration of corporate stocks and BSE licensing.
The BSE says it could service trade in corporate stocks of the mass privatisation programme even before being licensed but the commission has disagreed so far.

Bulgarians bought shares in 968 local companies against privatisation vouchers at the first tender of the country's mass sell-off programme in January. Shares in 204 firmes were sold out at the first tender.

Individuals and local privatisation funds can place bids for the second tender from March 21 through April 3. Shares in 830 firms with a total capital of 54 billion levs will be offered at the tender.
